name: UNICEF USA
mission: Over eight decades, the United Nations Children's Fund (UNICEF) has built an unprecedented global support system for the world's children. UNICEF relentlessly works day in and day out to deliver the essentials that give every child an equitable chance in life: health care and immunizations, safe water and sanitation, nutrition, education, emergency relief and more. UNICEF USA advances the global mission of UNICEF by rallying the American public to support the world's most vulnerable children. Together, we have helped save more children's lives than any other humanitarian organization.
theoryOfChange: The United Nations Children's Fund (UNICEF) works in more than 190 countries and territories to put children first. By providing access to health care, nutrition, clean water, education, protection and more, UNICEF empowers every child to have a brighter future. UNICEF USA supports UNICEF's work through fundraising, advocacy and education in the United States. Together, we are working toward the day when no children die from preventable causes, and every child has a safe and healthy childhood.

strengths_deep_dive: UNICEF USA exhibits efficient resource allocation, maintaining a cash-adjusted program ratio score based on a <cite id="1">78% cash-adjusted program ratio</cite> and an overall <cite id="1">Program expense ratio of 83.1%</cite>. This performance comfortably beats the 75% industry benchmark for humanitarian nonprofits. Institutional strength is further underscored by top-tier accountability scores, including a <cite id="1">99.36 rating on Charity Navigator's Accountability beacon</cite> and a Platinum Seal of Transparency from Candid. Furthermore, leadership maintains exceptional fundraising efficiency, expending only <cite id="1">$0.10 per $1 raised</cite>.
rich_narrative.summary: UNICEF USA supports global child health, nutrition, and emergency protection, directing significant funding toward child-focused interventions. In FY2025, the organization operated with a <cite id="3">Total Revenue of $835,217,861</cite>. Its financial discipline is reflected in a <cite id="1">Program expense ratio of 83.1%</cite>, which exceeds the 75% industry standard. The organization holds a strong <cite id="1">overall score of 97.0/100 from Charity Navigator</cite>, backed by robust governance practices and extensive international partner networks. While overall funding remains substantial, revenue experienced a recent contraction, falling from $829,050,932 in FY2023 to $720,404,955 in FY2024. Additionally, working capital reserves remain lean, providing approximately 2.8 months of operational coverage. Overall, UNICEF USA presents a positive profile with named caveats around revenue stabilization and reserve levels.
